"A **Venn diagram** is a collection of simple closed curves in the plane whose $n$ bounded regions correspond to all nonempty subsets of an $n$-element set; it is **non-simple** if some pair of curves intersects more than once or more than two curves pass through a common point. The associated planar graph has vertices at curve intersections and edges given by curve segments between consecutive intersections.

**Hamiltonicity conjecture.** Every non-simple Venn diagram has a Hamiltonian associated planar graph.

Hamiltonicity is known for simple Venn diagrams, while the statement for non-simple Venn diagrams remains open; the authors note that they know of no counterexamples and present this conjecture in the spirit of Winkler's conjecture."
